title: Pay‑Per‑Alert: Cutting On‑Call Costs with WakeUp Dev’s Unlimited‑Seat Model
description: Explore how WakeUp Dev’s pay‑per‑alert model eliminates per‑seat fees, reduces overhead, and keeps on‑call teams lean without sacrificing coverage.
author: Enrique Drack
topic: Pay‑Per‑Alert: Cutting On‑Call Costs with WakeUp Dev’s Unlimited‑Seat Model

blocks.text: Per‑seat licensing forces teams to pay for every on‑call member, even when the seat sits idle. For a 20‑person squad that’s 20 × $X/month, a cost that scales linearly with team size.

WakeUp Dev removes the per‑seat burden by charging only for the voice alerts that actually reach a responder. Each alert is a single API call to POST https://api.wakeupdev.com/v1/alert with your x‑api‑key. The cost is proportional to the number of alerts, not the number of seats.

items: Unlimited seats: add or remove team members without changing the bill.
No per‑seat tax: the platform’s pricing model is flat across all seats.

blocks.text: When Grafana fires an alert, the webhook payload is forwarded to WakeUp Dev, which then initiates a voice call to the on‑call rotation. The responder can ACK by pressing 1, ending the call instantly.

A typical 30‑person team that receives 5 k alerts per month can cut its on‑call budget from $4,800 (20 × $240) to roughly $100 (5 k × $0.02). The savings grow as alert volume rises, while the unlimited‑seat model keeps staffing flexible.
WakeUp Dev’s pay‑per‑alert pricing aligns cost with actual usage, giving SREs a clear financial incentive to optimize alert rules and reduce noise.
